rows.title: Auto Idle-Stop Failure to Restart (2016-2020 MDX)
rows.description: On 2016-2020 Acura MDX with the 3.5L V6 (J35Y5) and Auto Idle-Stop, the engine may fail to automatically restart from a stop event, leaving the driver stranded in traffic. rows.solution: Have dealer perform the PGM-FI idle-stop software update plus starter / starter relay inspection per Honda's 2023 service campaign (covered 10 years). To avoid recurrence, defeat Idle-Stop with the dash button each drive or install an aftermarket auto-disable module.

rows.title: First-Year 2001 MDX Included in NADI Driver Airbag Inflator Recall (NHTSA 20V026000)
rows.description: Only the 2001 model year of the Acura MDX falls under NHTSA recall 20V026000, the Non-Azide Driver airbag Inflator (NADI) campaign. This is a distinct problem from the PSAN-propellant inflator recalls — NADI inflators do not use phase stabilized ammonium nitrate at all. The defect is a manufacturing issue that lets the driver inflator take on moisture. In a crash severe enough to deploy the driver frontal airbag, that moisture can cause the inflator to rupture, sending metal fragments toward the driver and other people in the MDX, or it can cause the cushion to inflate only partially so it fails to protect the driver as designed. Both failure modes increase the chance of serious injury or death, which is why this is a safety recall rather than a service campaign. Honda's filing lists 1,439,841 vehicles for the entire campaign across all affected Honda, Acura and Isuzu models.
rows.solution: Take the MDX to an Acura dealer; the inspection and any repair are free. The dealer checks the driver frontal airbag inflator and replaces it with an inflator of a different design if it needs replacing. The recall began October 1, 2020. Because a 2001 MDX is likely on its second or third owner, don't rely on having received a letter — run the VIN through nhtsa.gov/recalls, or call American Honda's Customer Support & Campaign Center at 1-888-234-2138.

rows.title: 2020 XT6 Start/Stop Accumulator May Be Missing Endcap Bolts — Recall 20V668000
rows.description: Only the 2020 model year of the Cadillac XT6 falls inside this GM recall, which addresses a start/stop transmission accumulator that may have left the plant with bolts missing from its endcap. Because those bolts hold the endcap against transmission oil pressure, the missing hardware can allow a transmission oil leak. NHTSA's consequence statement is blunt about where that goes: the leak may progress to a loss of propulsion, increasing crash risk, and transmission fluid in the presence of an ignition source may increase the risk of fire. The same defect was found across a range of 2018-2020 Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac vehicles; the XT6's exposure is the 2020 year alone.
rows.solution: Free of charge at a Cadillac dealer: the technician inspects the start/stop transmission accumulator on your 2020 XT6 and replaces the unit if any endcap bolts are missing. The recall opened to owners on December 15, 2020. If you bought the XT6 used, do not assume the previous owner had it done — check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, then book the inspection through Cadillac customer service at 1-800-458-8006. GM's recall number is N202313440.

rows.title: 3.6L LGX Engine Oil Migrating Into the Cooling System Through Block Porosity — Overheating with Sludge in the Radiator
rows.description: GM bulletin 21-NA-108 (which superseded PIP5257E) covers engine overheating with the cooling system contaminated by engine oil, and it lists the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 with the 3.6L LGX V6 among the affected applications. The failure is not a head gasket in the usual sense: pressurized oil from the main oil gallery migrates into a coolant water jacket through porosity or a thin-wall casting defect in the engine block. Because oil pressure is far higher than coolant pressure, oil pushes into the coolant rather than the other way round, and the surge tank and radiator fill with a thick brown oil-and-coolant emulsion that looks like a milkshake. That emulsion will not carry heat, so the engine overheats, and it plugs the radiator and heater core. GM bulletins 21-NA-147 and 22-NA-240 cover the related diagnosis of a coolant and/or oil leak with the malfunction indicator lamp on. This is engine-code specific — it is an LGX 3.6L casting issue and is not a claim about the 2.0L LSY turbo four also sold in the XT6.
rows.solution: Do not just flush the coolant and refill — the contamination will come straight back. Follow the bulletin's diagnostic sequence, which confirms the source by pressure-testing and by checking whether the oil level drops while the coolant turns to emulsion. Where the leak path is traced to block porosity, the repair is an engine block or complete engine replacement, which is why this is worth pursuing under the 6-year/70,000-mile GM powertrain warranty while it is still in force; document the concern in writing at the first sign of contamination. If contamination is confirmed, the radiator, surge tank, heater core and oil cooler all need flushing or replacement, since emulsified oil coats every passage. Out of warranty an engine replacement on an XT6 typically runs $8,000-$12,000.
symptoms: Engine temperature climbing or overheat warning
Thick brown or tan milkshake-like sludge in the coolant surge tank and radiator
Engine oil level dropping with no external leak and no visible smoke
Weak or oily-smelling cabin heat as the heater core plugs

rows.title: Electric Power Steering Rack Failure — "Steering Assist Is Reduced / Service Power Steering" with C0460 or C0545
rows.description: XT6 owners report a "Steering Assist is Reduced — Drive with Care" or "Service Power Steering" message in the driver information center, usually with a noticeable increase in steering effort. GM bulletin 20-NA-215 covers this condition on the XT5 and XT6 and ties it to DTCs C0460 and/or C0545 stored in the power steering module. The XT6 uses a belt-drive electric rack with the motor and control module integrated into the steering gear, so an internal fault or a torque-sensor signal fault sets the code and the module deliberately cuts or reduces assist rather than allowing erratic assist. Steering is still mechanically connected — the car remains steerable — but effort rises sharply, which is most alarming at parking-lot speeds or in an evasive maneuver. Owners also describe a separate, milder version where assist fades after sustained low-speed maneuvering and returns once the system cools; that thermal derate is normal protection, not a failed rack, and it clears itself.
rows.solution: Have the power steering module scanned first. A stored C0460 or C0545 per bulletin 20-NA-215 calls for replacement of the complete steering gear assembly — the module is not serviced separately. After the rack is replaced the steering angle sensor must be recalibrated with a capable scan tool or the system will not function and the message will return. Out of warranty a rack and calibration typically runs roughly $1,500-$2,600 at a dealer. Before replacing anything, rule out the thermal derate (assist returns after cooling, no stored code) and a weak battery or poor ground, either of which can trigger a false assist-reduced message on this platform. The XT6's powertrain warranty does not cover this, but the 4-year/50,000-mile bumper-to-bumper coverage does.
symptoms: "Steering Assist is Reduced — Drive with Care" message in the DIC
Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at parking speeds
Assist cuts out intermittently and returns after a restart
Sometimes accompanied by other electrical warnings on the same drive

rows.title: Incorrect Transmission Sun Gear Lets the Driver-Side Half-Shaft Disengage — Recall 23V172
rows.description: NHTSA campaign 23V172000 (GM safety recall N222389310) covers 613 model-year 2023 Cadillac XT6 vehicles built with an incorrect sun gear inside the transmission's final drive. The wrong gear does not retain the driver-side (left front) half-shaft correctly, and the shaft can disengage from the transmission. Two failure modes follow: while driving, the wheel stops receiving torque and the vehicle loses drive power; while parked, the park pawl can no longer hold the vehicle through a disengaged shaft, so the XT6 can roll away even with the shifter in Park. The same wrong-gear condition was recalled on the Cadillac XT5, Chevrolet Blazer and Traverse, and GMC Acadia, but confirm your own VIN rather than assuming a sibling's campaign applies.
rows.solution: A free recall remedy exists. Dealers replace the sun gears at no charge under NHTSA 23V172000 / GM N222389310; owner letters were mailed May 1, 2023. Until the repair is done, always set the parking brake when parking. If drive power has already been lost, have the vehicle towed rather than driven — a fully disengaged half-shaft will not propel the car and can damage the transmission case.

rows.title: Instrument Panel Fails to Illuminate Hazard, High-Beam and Turn-Signal Telltales — Software Recall 24V459
rows.description: NHTSA campaign 24V459000 covers late-build Cadillac XT6 vehicles on which the instrument panel cluster may not illuminate when the hazard warning lights, high beams, or turn signals are activated. The exterior lamps themselves still work — the failure is the driver's feedback. That matters because a driver who cannot see the high-beam indicator may leave the brights on and blind oncoming traffic, and a driver who cannot see the turn-signal telltale may leave a signal running or believe the hazards are off when the vehicle is stopped on a shoulder. This is a software defect in the instrument cluster, not a bulb or wiring failure.

Dealers update the instrument panel cluster software at no charge under NHTSA 24V459000; owner letters were expected August 5, 2024. If your XT6 exhibits the symptom, check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls before paying anyone to diagnose a cluster — replacing the cluster is not the fix and is not necessary.

rows.title: Loss of Cabin Heat Caused by an Engine Control Module Software Anomaly — Bulletin 22-NA-094
rows.description: GM bulletin 22-NA-094, issued July 2022, addresses a loss of cabin heat on the Cadillac XT6 and XT5. Owners get little or no warm air from the vents even after the engine reaches operating temperature — the complaint typically shows up in cold weather and is easy to misdiagnose as a stuck thermostat, an air pocket in the cooling system, a blend door actuator, or a plugged heater core. GM traced it instead to a software anomaly in the engine control module: the ECM's thermal management strategy does not bring coolant temperature up or route flow to the heater core as intended, so the heater has nothing hot to work with. Because the fault is calibration rather than hardware, no part is actually broken, and owners who let a shop chase it mechanically can spend hundreds of dollars replacing a perfectly good thermostat or heater core before the real fix is applied.
rows.solution: The fix is a reprogram, not a part. Per bulletin 22-NA-094, the correction is to reprogram the engine control module with the updated calibration; this is a dealer or capable-shop operation using GM's programming tools and takes about an hour. Ask specifically for bulletin 22-NA-094 by number. Before authorizing a thermostat or heater core replacement for a no-heat complaint on an XT6, confirm the ECM calibration is current — under the 4-year/50,000-mile bumper-to-bumper warranty the reprogram is free, and even out of warranty it typically runs $100-$200 against $600-$1,400 for a heater core job that would not have fixed it.
symptoms: Little or no heat from the vents in cold weather
Cabin takes an unusually long time to warm up, or never does
Engine coolant temperature gauge reads normal while the vents blow cool

rows.title: Recall 22V446000: Fuel Tank Rollover Valve May Fail to Seal on 2022 XT6
rows.description: Certain 2022 Cadillac XT6 crossovers were recalled by General Motors for a fuel tank rollover valve that may not seal properly in a rollover crash. NHTSA files the defect against the gasoline storage tank assembly. The rollover valve's whole purpose is to shut the tank's vent path when the XT6 is no longer upright, keeping gasoline inside the tank rather than letting it run out through the vent. On the recalled vehicles the valve can be dislodged from its position or absent altogether, which leaves nothing to close that path. GM's stated consequence is direct: fuel can leak during a rollover crash, and that raises the risk of a fire. This is not a drivability problem — the XT6 runs and refuels normally with the defect present, which is exactly why it is worth confirming by VIN rather than waiting to notice something wrong.

rows.title: Water Leaks Into the Interior Through Pinholes in the Roof Panel Laser Braze — Wet Carpet and Inoperative Liftgate Actuator
rows.description: GM bulletin 19-NA-167 covers water leaking into the interior on the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 (alongside the 2017-2021 XT5 and GMC Acadia). Owners find wet carpet or headliner at the front and/or rear, on either side, typically after rain or a car wash. The cause is not the sunroof drains that owners and shops usually chase first: it is pinhole voids in the laser braze joint between the roof panel and the outer body ring, and in the seam sealer over it. The bulletin says the pinholes are most often found near the top of the windshield at the A-pillars, or near the top of the liftgate at the D-pillars. Water entering at the D-pillars runs down into the rear of the vehicle, and the bulletin specifically notes that on the XT6 the liftgate actuator may become noisy or inoperative as a result — so an electrical complaint at the tailgate is a symptom of the body leak, not a separate failure. Left alone, trapped water rots carpet padding, grows mold, and corrodes rear body connectors.
rows.solution: Have the shop follow 19-NA-167 rather than starting with sunroof drain cleaning. The diagnosis is a water test of the roof-to-body laser braze at the A-pillar and D-pillar corners to find the pinholes, followed by resealing the braze joint and seam sealer at the void. Any water-damaged carpet and padding must be lifted and fully dried, and a liftgate actuator that has been soaked usually needs replacement even after the leak is sealed. Expect roughly $300-$1,200 for the leak repair and drying at a dealer, more if the actuator or a wet module has to be replaced; this is a factory body-sealing defect, so ask about warranty coverage before authorizing a paid repair.

rows.title: 8F35 8-speed automatic shudder, buck, and jerk under 35 mph
rows.description: Nautilus models built on or before March 11, 2021 with the 8F35 8-speed automatic commonly exhibit a shudder, buck, hesitation, or jerk while accelerating from a stop up to about 35 mph (57 km/h). Ford Technical Service Bulletin 21-2389 (superseding 21-2081) attributes the condition primarily to PCM/transmission solenoid control software rather than internal mechanical wear, though severe untreated cases progressed to harsh shifting and, in a minority of CarComplaints reports, complete transmission failure. rows.title: Panoramic Sunroof Spontaneously Shattering / Exploding
rows.description: Muranos equipped with the factory panoramic glass roof have a documented history of the glass spontaneously shattering or 'exploding' with a loud bang, often while driving or even while parked, with no external impact. NHTSA began receiving complaints as early as 2008, and the Murano was among the most-cited models in a certified class-action lawsuit (Johnson et al. v. Nissan North America) covering 2009-2020 model years. The alleged cause is a tight factory seal plus tempered/ceramic-painted glass that builds stress until ordinary driving conditions trigger fracture.
rows.solution: Because there is no recall, repair is typically owner-paid: replacement of the panoramic glass panel runs roughly $500-$1,500+ depending on whether OEM glass and a new seal are used. Affected owners have pursued reimbursement through the class-action settlement and homeowner/auto glass insurance. Some owners apply protective film as a mitigation against injury from flying glass.
symptoms: Loud bang or explosion sound from the roof
Glass roof shatters with no impact

rows.title: Recall 21V402000: Weak Steering Knuckle or Rear Axle Housing From Improper Heat-Treatment
rows.description: If you own a 2020 Nissan Murano, it may fall under NHTSA recall 21V402000. The front steering knuckle or the rear axle housing on affected vehicles was not heat-treated correctly, which leaves it with insufficient strength. The practical risk Nissan describes is an impact — the example given is hitting a curb — deforming the part. A deformed steering knuckle can cost you steering control; a deformed rear axle can allow a wheel to separate. Either raises the risk of a crash. The recall population is 14,276 vehicles for the entire campaign, which also covers several other Nissan and INFINITI models.
rows.solution: Take the Murano to a Nissan dealer for the free recall repair. The dealer inspects the front steering knuckle and rear axle housing and replaces whichever is necessary at no charge to you. Owner letters were mailed July 26, 2021. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see whether the remedy has already been performed on your specific vehicle, and call Nissan customer service at 1-800-867-7669 with questions or if a dealer cannot schedule you.

rows.title: Sunroof Drain or Roof Area Water Intrusion Causing Wet Headliner/Carpet and Electrical Issues
rows.description: Murano owners continue to report water leaks into the cabin, often showing up as damp headliner edges, wet front footwells, musty odor, or water near A-pillars after rain or car washes. The most common causes are restricted sunroof drains, disconnected drain tubes, or seal/body seam issues around the roof opening area. If ignored, the leak can damage carpet padding, connectors, and interior electronics.
rows.solution: Water-test the roof and windshield perimeter while inspecting the sunroof cassette drains and A-pillar drain routing. Clear clogged drains with low-pressure air or line, repair or reconnect drain tubes, and inspect for seal or seam leaks if drains flow normally. Dry the carpet and underlayment thoroughly afterward to prevent mold and corrosion in connectors under the carpet.

rows.title: Timing Chain / Guide Rattle on Startup (2nd Gen)
rows.description: Second-generation Muranos commonly develop a ticking or rattling noise at startup, lasting more than a couple of seconds, caused by worn timing chain guides/tensioners that create slack in the chain. The condition is aggravated by extended oil-change intervals or low oil. If ignored, a stretched chain or failed guide can cause timing-related running problems and potential valve damage.
rows.solution: Maintain short, on-time oil changes with the correct viscosity to preserve tensioner pressure. If the rattle persists, have the timing chain, guides, and tensioners professionally replaced. Confirm proper oil pressure and check for sludge that can starve the tensioner.

rows.title: Transfer Case Seal Leak (AWD Models)

If the transfer case has been run low on fluid, the coupling may need replacement ($800-1,500). In severe cases, the entire transfer case assembly needs replacement ($1,500-2,500). Check transfer case fluid level at every oil change as preventive maintenance.

rows.title: VQ35DE 3.5L Excessive Oil Consumption
rows.description: The first-generation Murano's VQ35DE 3.5L V6 is known for high oil consumption as it ages, often well before 100,000 miles. Owners report burning roughly a quart every 1,000-2,500 miles (worse in some cases). The cause is attributed to piston ring sealing problems against slightly tapered cylinder bores, producing blow-by; some owners also report oil pooling in the intake/PCV hoses. Left unchecked, low oil accelerates timing chain and bearing wear.
rows.solution: Monitor oil level frequently and top up between changes; replace/clean the PCV valve and oil-fouled hoses. Verified repairs include updated piston ring sets (an engine re-ring) or, in severe cases, engine replacement — both costly. Using the correct oil grade/viscosity and shorter change intervals slows consumption.
